faqs.q: What is the biggest expense of living in Gurgaon?
faqs.a: Housing is by far the biggest expense in Gurgaon, whether you pay rent or a home loan EMI, and it varies sharply between prime areas and newer outer sectors. After that come transport, electricity bills that rise in summer because of air conditioning, eating out and, for families, school fees.

faqs.q: Which are the more affordable areas to live in Gurgaon?
faqs.a: Newer and outer areas such as Sohna Road, New Gurgaon and sectors like Sector 70 usually offer cheaper housing than prime locations like Golf Course Road and the area around DLF Cyber City. The trade-off can be a longer commute, so check travel time to your office before choosing.

faqs.q: Do I need a car to live in Gurgaon?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. The Delhi Metro and the Rapid Metro cover parts of Gurgaon, and autos and app cabs are easy to find. But many newer sectors are far from a metro station and last-mile options can be patchy, so people living there often rely on cabs or their own vehicle.

faqs.q: Is Gurgaon the same as Gurugram?
faqs.a: Yes. The Haryana government officially renamed the city Gurugram in 2016, but both names are still widely used, especially Gurgaon in everyday speech. Addresses, government records and property documents now generally use Gurugram.
